David Lisnard is the French 🇫🇷 Milei and here's why he could win the French presidential election.

Lisnard’s argument is brutally simple: France does not have a management problem. It has a state problem.

Too much spending. Too much tax. Too much bureaucracy. Too many rules. Too many people paid to administer systems that increasingly fail to deliver. His answer is not another reform commission. It is the chainsaw.

Milei became powerful when voters stopped asking, “How do we improve the system?” and started asking, “Why are we still protecting it?” Lisnard is betting that France is approaching the same psychological point.

He also occupies a space almost nobody else really owns. Macronism offers technocracy. The traditional right offers caution. The RN offers nationalism mixed with economic statism. 

Lisnard offers something much cleaner: order, capitalism, deregulation, lower taxes and a smaller state.

And he has one advantage over the professional protest politician: he has governed. Cannes gives him a concrete executive record and allows him to say: this is not a television theory. I have actually run something.

His opportunity comes the day the French stop believing that another adjustment will save the model.

Because once voters conclude that the machine itself is broken, the man holding the wrench suddenly becomes much less interesting than the man holding the chainsaw.

• The launch of Operation Dawn of Yemen comes within the framework of the Yemeni government’s transition to exercising its responsibilities in reclaiming the remaining territories of the Republic and extending the authority of the state and its institutions. It is not an option separate from the political process or an alternative to peace. Rather, it came after the exhaustion of the various available peaceful means and opportunities, amid the continued approach of the terrorist Houthi militias of escalation, mobilization, threats, and repeated attacks, their refusal to respond to de-escalation efforts, their continued expansion of armed control within the country, and the serious and grave violations in their practices, in a manner that threatens Yemen’s unity and sovereignty and undermines the prospects of reaching a sustainable peace. Previous experiences, in particular, have demonstrated that temporary truces or arrangements that do not address the roots of the problem do not put an end to it.
• His Excellency the President directed the security agencies and all participating formations to adhere strictly to the law, protect civilians and their property, and prevent acts of vengeance or retaliation, stressing that the objective is not limited to reclaiming territory, but also includes restoring the state and its institutions to it and reaching Sana’a.
• The government renewed its offer of safe return and amnesty to everyone who lays down their weapons, ceases fighting in the ranks of the Iranian-backed Houthi militias, and returns to their family. It called on residents in areas of operations to stay away from military sites, gatherings, and supply routes for their safety.
• In this context, the Embassy of the Republic of Yemen in Vienna affirms that the current developments cannot be viewed merely as an internal Yemeni affair. The Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has witnessed increasing military escalation over recent weeks, represents one of the most important maritime corridors linking Asia and Europe through the Red Sea and the Suez Canal. Any persistent threat to this corridor has repercussions for international maritime security, shipping and insurance costs, energy markets, and global supply chains.
• From this standpoint, the restoration of the Yemeni state’s control over its coasts, ports, and territorial waters represents an essential part of any sustainable solution for the security of the Red Sea. Warships and defense systems can deal with an immediate threat, but lasting security for maritime corridors begins with the existence of a state capable of protecting its territory and coasts and holding exclusive authority over weapons and the decision on war and peace.

text:
Three places get offered as proof that giants were real. All three places are real. What they prove is not the same.

Lovelock Cave, Nevada. A real cave, dug out for bat guano in 1911, then excavated by Llewellyn Loud in 1912 and again with Harrington in 1924. The giants come from later retellings. Sarah Winnemucca Hopkins, the 1883 source, tells of an enemy tribe her people fought and trapped in a cave. She does not call them giants.

Judaculla Rock, North Carolina. A real soapstone boulder covered in petroglyphs, pre modern but not securely dated. Cherokee tradition holds that Tsul'kalu left marks on it. The link comes from tradition, not from anything in the stone.

Budj Bim, Victoria. A real volcano, and in Gunditjmara tradition an ancestral being who revealed himself in the landscape. Geological dating puts the eruption at roughly 37,000 years ago, and Gunditjmara people were there. The giant is the mountain, and the memory lines up with the geology.

A cave that never had giants in it, a rock that carries a name, and a mountain that is a person, remembered. Only the third is a match between story and evidence, and careful writers still call it alignment, not proof.

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

MFFU PERPS — MORNING REGIME RADAR
6 OCT 2026
MAIN CONCLUSION: The first European session of the day finds crypto in consolidation rather than confirmed expansion. Bitcoin has once again failed to establish acceptance above the $87K area and is trading back near the mid-$85K region, while ETH and SOL remain constructive but softer. The most important positive signal is that leverage still looks controlled rather than euphoric.
For traders interested in experiencing this 24/7 perpetual-market model through a prop structure, MyFundedPerps offers access to a broad universe of perpetual markets. A 20% discount can be applied when purchasing an eligible plan using Code: NQRADAR, subject to confirmation at checkout.
BTC IS STILL FIGHTING THE SAME RESISTANCE
Bitcoin has again tested the $87K area and failed to convert it into confirmed support. That makes the structure increasingly clear: the $87K–$87.5K zone remains the breakout gate, while the current mid-$85K region continues to act as the market's short-term equilibrium.
The important detail is that repeated rejection has not yet produced a structural breakdown. BTC continues to hold a sequence of higher short-term lows beneath horizontal resistance. That means compression is increasing rather than disappearing.
Compression eventually resolves. The market has simply not confirmed the direction yet.
$87K MATTERS MORE THAN THE DAILY PERCENTAGE MOVE
BTC being modestly lower over 24 hours matters less than the location of that weakness. Price attempted to leave the range and sellers absorbed the move.
That gives traders useful information.
If BTC attacks $87K again with stronger participation, stable funding and improving breadth, the probability of eventual acceptance increases. If every new attempt produces immediate rejection and progressively weaker rebounds, the resistance becomes more meaningful rather than less.
For now, $87K remains supply until the market proves otherwise.
HIGHER LOWS ARE KEEPING THE BULLISH CASE ALIVE
The bearish interpretation would be much stronger if each rejection from $87K were followed by a fresh local low. That has not happened.
Instead, BTC continues to compress between rising support and horizontal resistance. That is a constructive structure, even if it remains unresolved.
The bullish path is still a higher low followed by another resistance test and eventual acceptance. The bearish path begins only if the rising support structure breaks and the market starts producing lower lows beneath the current balance zone.
Until one of those paths develops, patience remains part of the edge.
FUNDING IS NOT SHOWING EUPHORIA
One of the most important derivatives signals this morning is what is not happening.
Funding across the major BTC perpetual venues remains mildly positive to near neutral rather than aggressively stretched. That means traders are not yet paying extreme premiums to stay long beneath resistance.
This is healthier than a market where price stalls while leveraged longs continue piling in.
The current message is therefore closer to controlled positioning than speculative overcrowding.
That reduces the probability of an immediate leverage-driven flush, although it does not eliminate the risk if price structure deteriorates.
OPEN INTEREST ALSO REMAINS CONTROLLED
Aggregate BTC open interest is broadly stable rather than accelerating aggressively into the resistance zone.
That distinction matters.
A market where price stalls, open interest rises sharply and funding becomes increasingly positive is vulnerable because leverage is expanding faster than price.
That is not the dominant structure at the moment.
The current pullback looks more like consolidation and profit-taking than an obvious derivatives instability.
For perp traders, that means the breakout remains possible without the market first requiring a major leverage reset.
ETH IS STILL THE FIRST ROTATION TEST
ETH remains around the $2.7K area and continues to hold its broader structure despite modest weakness.
Ethereum matters because it is the first meaningful test of whether capital is willing to rotate beyond Bitcoin.
If BTC stabilises and ETH begins outperforming again, the quality of the broader crypto market improves. If ETH weakens materially against BTC while Bitcoin itself begins losing support, the market becomes more defensive.
The absolute ETH price matters, but the relative relationship between ETH and BTC matters more for judging rotation.
SOL REMAINS THE CLEANEST LIQUID-BETA SIGNAL
SOL continues to trade around the $120 region and remains one of the most useful instruments for measuring liquid high-beta appetite.
Its position is especially interesting because leverage remains relatively restrained compared with more speculative parts of the market.
If SOL begins advancing while BTC remains stable and funding stays controlled, that would support the idea that risk appetite is broadening without becoming overcrowded.
If SOL starts breaking down while BTC remains trapped below $87K, it would be an early indication that traders are reducing beta beneath the surface.
ALTCOIN DISPERSION IS THE REAL STORY
The market is not moving as one block.
Some higher-beta assets continue to show meaningful relative strength while several majors remain softer. That is not a classic broad altseason structure.
It is dispersion.
And dispersion can be highly useful for perp traders because relative strength becomes more informative than simply asking whether crypto is up or down.
The strongest asset is not always the best trade, but persistent outperformance while BTC is consolidating can reveal where capital is actually moving.
HYPE REMAINS AN IMPORTANT SENTIMENT GAUGE
HYPE continues to be useful as a derivatives-native measure of speculative appetite.
If HYPE stays firm while ETH and SOL stabilise, higher-beta participation remains alive. If HYPE begins reversing sharply while BTC is still below resistance, it may indicate that traders are reducing speculative exposure before the core market itself weakens.
That makes HYPE valuable not only as a tradable asset, but also as a warning instrument for the broader perp complex.
BNB IS SENDING A DIFFERENT MESSAGE
BNB has been weaker than several other large-cap crypto assets, but the weakness has not been accompanied by an obvious explosion in leveraged positioning.
That distinction matters.
Price weakness with declining or stable open interest often reflects traders reducing exposure rather than building an aggressive directional bet.
Again, this supports the idea that the market is currently selective rather than systemically risk-off.
THE MACRO BACKDROP IS STILL DIFFICULT
Traditional markets are fully active again, and crypto is no longer trading in isolation.
The US 10Y remains around the 5.3% region, while the dollar remains firm. Those conditions are not naturally supportive for speculative assets because they keep global financial conditions tight.
At the same time, oil has moved lower and Nasdaq remains near record territory. Those factors provide an important offset.
The result is a mixed macro environment rather than a clearly bearish one.
BTC IS CURRENTLY LAGGING NQ
One of today's most interesting divergences is that Nasdaq remains close to record territory while Bitcoin continues struggling below $87K.
That tells us crypto is not simply following technology beta.
If NQ remains strong and BTC eventually breaks resistance, crypto would be catching up with the broader risk regime.
If NQ continues making highs while BTC repeatedly fails, the weakness becomes increasingly crypto-specific.
That divergence deserves close attention because it helps identify whether the problem is global macro pressure or internal crypto positioning.
THE US 10Y STILL MATTERS FOR PERPS
A crypto trader does not need to trade Treasuries, but ignoring the US 10Y in the current environment is a mistake.
At around 5.3%, the long end represents a substantial opportunity cost for speculative capital.
If yields begin easing while Nasdaq remains strong, the backdrop for crypto improves. If the 10Y breaks materially higher while DXY strengthens, BTC's $87K ceiling becomes harder to overcome.
The cleanest bullish macro structure would be NQ firm, the 10Y stable or lower, the dollar contained and BTC finally accepting above resistance.
LOWER OIL IS HELPING
Brent below the recent psychological $100 area and WTI below $90 remove one source of inflation pressure.
That matters indirectly for crypto because lower energy prices can reduce pressure on inflation expectations and long-term yields.
In the current regime, every macro force that helps stabilise the long end improves the environment for risk assets.
Oil does not determine Bitcoin, but in a 5%+ Treasury world, it matters more than usual.
TODAY'S MACRO CALENDAR STILL MATTERS
The US session brings trade data, Fed commentary and later a Treasury auction.
None of these events is guaranteed to dominate crypto by itself.
But their effect on yields, the dollar and Nasdaq can materially change the backdrop for BTC and the broader perp market.
For today, the macro hierarchy remains simple: watch the 10Y, DXY and NQ first, then observe whether BTC confirms or rejects the external signal.
THE US CASH OPEN REMAINS A LIQUIDITY TRANSITION
Crypto trades 24/7, but liquidity quality changes when the US session becomes active.
Institutional participation increases, ETF-related flows become more relevant, and traditional markets provide live confirmation.
That means a move during the European morning does not carry the same information as a move during peak US liquidity.
For perp traders, the early session is often preparation. The US window is where confirmation becomes more reliable.
MFFU PERPS REQUIRES SELECTIVITY, NOT CONSTANT ACTIVITY
The ability to trade 24/7 does not mean a trader should remain positioned 24/7.
The real advantage of perpetuals is access to continuous opportunity.
That only becomes useful if the trader remains selective.
BTC, ETH and SOL provide deep liquidity. HYPE, ADA, AVAX, SUI, LINK, DOGE and other supported assets provide additional beta and dispersion.
But the correct market is the one offering the best risk-adjusted structure, not simply the largest candle.
RELATIVE STRENGTH MAY BE THE BEST EDGE TODAY
Because BTC remains compressed below resistance while individual alts diverge sharply, today's best opportunity may come from relative strength rather than trying to predict the entire market.
An alt holding gains while BTC weakens modestly is giving information.
An alt failing to rise while BTC strengthens is also giving information.
SOL outperforming ETH, HYPE remaining strong while other high-beta assets weaken, or selected names refusing to break support can all reveal positioning before the broader chart becomes obvious.
This is exactly the kind of environment where selective perp trading can outperform indiscriminate directional exposure.
BULLISH SCENARIO — ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE: 57%
The bullish case requires BTC to preserve its sequence of higher lows and attack $87K again.
Funding remains controlled, open interest does not become excessively leveraged, ETH stabilises, SOL regains momentum and higher-beta leaders continue to hold relative strength.
The external macro confirmation would be Nasdaq remaining firm while Treasury yields stop accelerating and the dollar remains contained.
A clean BTC acceptance above $87K would move the market from compression into expansion.
BEARISH SCENARIO — ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE: 43%
The bearish case begins with another rejection from $87K followed by the loss of rising support.
If BTC moves lower while ETH/BTC weakens, SOL loses its current support structure and high-beta leadership fades, the internal market becomes significantly less healthy.
The signal becomes stronger if NQ weakens at the same time that the 10Y and DXY move higher.
That would transform consolidation into a genuine risk-off regime.
ANALYTICAL EDGE
BULLISH: 57%
BEARISH: 43%
EDGE: SLIGHTLY BULLISH — COMPRESSION, NOT CONFIRMED BREAKOUT.
The structure still slightly favours bulls because BTC continues to hold higher lows while leverage remains reasonably controlled.
But repeated failures around $87K cannot be ignored.
The market must prove that buyers can absorb the supply sitting there.
Until that happens, leverage should respect the range rather than anticipate the breakout.
CURRENT REGIME
CURRENT REGIME: BTC COMPRESSION BELOW MAJOR RESISTANCE / CONTROLLED LEVERAGE / HIGH ALTCOIN DISPERSION / FULL MACRO RECONNECTION.
Bitcoin is not breaking down.
It is also not breaking out.
ETH and SOL remain constructive but cautious, while selected higher-beta assets continue to show stronger relative performance.
Funding and open interest are not signalling excessive leverage, which keeps the structure relatively healthy.
But the market remains unresolved until BTC proves it can hold above the $87K resistance zone.
FINAL ANALYTICAL VIEW
Tuesday begins with one exceptionally clean message for perpetual traders: do not confuse activity with direction.
Crypto is active. Individual alts are moving. Leverage is available. But Bitcoin itself is still negotiating the same resistance that has controlled the market for several sessions.
That makes BTC's compression more important than the excitement elsewhere.
The positive aspect is that derivatives positioning does not appear euphoric. Funding remains restrained and open interest is not exploding. That gives the market room to move if real demand finally absorbs $87K.
The negative aspect is equally clear. Repeated failed breakout attempts mean sellers are real.
The next attack needs better quality, ideally supported by ETH and SOL participation, controlled leverage and a macro environment in which Nasdaq remains firm while Treasury yields stabilise.
Until then, the best perp opportunities may continue to come from relative strength and selective rotation, rather than from making a large directional bet on the entire crypto complex.
BTC defines systemic direction. ETH measures rotation. SOL measures liquid beta. HYPE and the stronger alts show where speculative demand is concentrating. The US 10Y, DXY and NQ determine whether global financial conditions support or fight the move.
That is today's map.
Trade the strongest structure, not the loudest candle.

FOUNDATIONAL BLACK AMERICA – PURSUING ETHNORACIAL PURITY AT THE EXPENSE OF POWER

An individual or a group pursuing their own identity can be interpreted as a sign of independence, self-awareness and maturity, suggesting they may be expanding beyond their cognitive baseline.

The self-view of the FBA (Foundational Black Americans) interest group is a normative perspective but is fashioned as binary framing. The new identity which seeks the noble goal of indigenization for American Blacks, which while factual, is foolishly pursued at the cost of fragmentation.

While I accept the premise that Black Americans are indigenous to the nation called the United States of America, I insist that the FBA movement like the BLM organization is nothing more than a grift.
Blacks once the largest minority group in the US have now been surpassed by Latin Americans whose numbers draw from a vast human pool ranging from Mexico in the Argentina in the south, where Blacks who were one third of that country’s population have been exterminated as a race. Black Americans as a matter of sheer demographics cannot compete with the rates of Latin growth.

Secondly, Latin migrants are not sympathetic to Black American causes as Blacks in Latin countries generally face discrimination and occupy the bottom tiers of the socio-economic scale.
The polarizing FBA strategy which divides Blacks based on background is asinine and idiotic. It seeks a phony ethnic and racial purity at the expense of power. And so once again, Anglophone Black Americans, who are the modern founders of democracy stand to be cheated out their legacy and heritage in the American and Americas Projects because like Moonshine, the FBA fools who divide the Anglophone Black nation are likely bought and paid to pretend they have tails and to make monkey sounds because a political party that collapse the nation’s borders have greased and promised them “reparations” once they return to power and this talk of foundational blackness is simply positioning for the time when “reparations” will begin to flow and their goal is to ensure that they and only themselves get paid while Gambol and his kin don’t get so much as a nickel for his non-native Haitian or Jamaican grandma, which brings me back to my original point that the whole thing is just a grift.

On a more serious note, regarding the makeup and origins of Black Americans I’ve added the following regarding the foundational roots.

Historical records documenting the migration of enslaved people from the Caribbean to the British mainland colonies are vast, though they vary wildly depending on the colony, the century, and the nature of the trade.
Because the movement of enslaved people within the Americas—often called the Intra-American slave trade—frequently involved individual colonial merchants, smuggling, and personal property transfers, the paper trail is distinct from the larger transatlantic trade. Historians and genealogists rely on several specific types of records to track this history:
1. Database and Shipping Registries
·
· The Trans-Atlantic and Intra-American Slave Trade Databases: Hosted on https://t.co/wjEUg2pxF3, these massive public databases aggregate centuries of shipping manifests, custom house records, and port logs. The Intra-American Database specifically tracks thousands of documented coastal voyages that brought enslaved people from Caribbean ports (like Bridgetown, Barbados, or Kingston, Jamaica) to North American ports like Charleston, Boston, New York, and Chesapeake Bay. [1, 2, 3]
· Port Custom House Books: Colonial ports required captains to declare their cargo to collect taxes. For example, British "Naval Office Shipping Lists" record the arrivals of ships from the West Indies into ports like New York and Boston, listing cargo counts of sugar, molasses, rum, and "Negroes."
·
2. Early Settler Manifests and "Headright" Grants
In the southern colonies, particularly South Carolina, enslaved people from the Caribbean were frequently brought over not by slave traders, but as the personal property of migrating plantation owners. [1, 4]
·
· Headright Records: To encourage settlement, the "Lords Proprietors" of South Carolina offered white settlers land grants based on the number of dependents and enslaved people they brought with them (e.g., 20 acres per enslaved male, 10 per female). Land patent books and warrant registries explicitly record the names of white Barbadian planters claiming acreage for the enslaved Afro-Barbadians they brought to Charles Town in the 1670s. [5, 6, 7]
· Letters and Official Dispatches: Personal logs and letters from colonial officials capture these arrivals. For instance, historical documents note that South Carolina's first governor, William Sayle, brought four Black people with him from the Caribbean in 1670. Later that year, Captain Henry Brayne documented returning from a supply run with "one lusty negro man". [4, 5, 8]
·
3. State and Local Legal Archives
Because enslaved people were legally classified as property, their forced migration is heavily documented in local civil records rather than humanitarian ones: [9]
·
· Bills of Sale and Deeds: Local county courthouses hold property deeds recording the sale of enslaved individuals who were explicitly noted as "seasoned" (meaning they had already survived the disease environment and forced labor system of the Caribbean) or "born in the West Indies."
· Probate and Wills: Wealthy planters moving between the islands and the mainland left meticulous wills. A Barbadian planter might leave his estate in Barbados to one son, but bequeath "ten Negroes now serving on my plantation in Carolina" to another.
·
4. Newspaper Advertisements
·
· Runaway Slave Ads: In the 1700s, colonial newspapers (like the South Carolina Gazette or The Boston News-Letter) regularly published ads for escaped enslaved people. Masters frequently included critical biographical details to aid capture, writing descriptions such as: "Spokes English with a West India accent," "Lately imported from Jamaica," or "Is known to have family in Barbados."
· Auction and Cargo Notices:Merchants placed prominent ads announcing the arrival of ships from the Caribbean, listing items like "A prime parcel of Negroes, chiefly boys and girls, seasoned to the West Indies." [10]
·
5. Former British Colonies Enslavement Registers (1812–1834)
Though compiled much later—after the British abolished the international slave trade in 1807—the British government mandated meticulous registries to track the enslaved population in its colonies to prevent illegal smuggling. Available through resources like the National Archives (UK)and , these registers record an individual's name, age, owner, and crucially, whether they were born in Africa or the Caribbean, allowing historians to retroactively trace family lines that shifted between the islands and the mainland. [11, 12]

The first recorded arrivals of enslaved people from Barbados to the mainland American colonies occurred in two distinct historic waves, depending on the region:
1. The Earliest Arrival: Boston, Massachusetts (1638)
The very first documented arrival of enslaved Africans from Barbados to a mainland British colony occurred in New England. [1]
·
· The Ship: In February 1638, the built-in-America slave ship named the Desire sailed into Boston Harbor.
· The Cargo: After a voyage to the West Indies, the ship returned to Massachusetts carrying a cargo of salt, cotton, tobacco, and enslaved Africans purchased in Barbados. [1]
·
2. The Systemic Plantation Arrival: Charleston, South Carolina (1670)
While 1638 marks the earliest recorded arrival, the foundational arrival that imported the "Barbados Blueprint" (the systemic plantation model) to the American South occurred three decades later. [2]
·
· The Founding Voyage: In April 1670, the ship Carolina arrived at Albemarle Point to establish Charles Towne (Charleston) on behalf of England. [3, 4]
· The Scale: Over half of South Carolina’s original white settlers migrated directly from Barbados, and they brought enslaved Africans with them to clear the land and construct the new colony. [5, 6]
· The Impact: This 1670 arrival immediately implemented Barbadian chattel slavery on mainland soil, establishing South Carolina as the first colony engineered from its inception as a dedicated "slave society". [7, 8]

Estimating the exact percentage of enslaved people in the United States who descended from West Indian slaves requires looking at two different figures: the raw percentage of arrivals from the Caribbean versus the generational exponential growth (the "founder effect") of those early populations.
While only 13% to 15%of all enslaved people brought to mainland North America arrived via the West Indies, the timeline of their arrival means that by 1860, the vast majority (potentially 50% to 75%+) of the enslaved population in the American South likely carried West Indian ancestry. [1]
The breakdown of this historical estimate involves several key factors:
1. The Importation Percentage (13% – 15%)
According to data from the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database, the total number of enslaved Africans who arrived in what is now the United States is estimated at roughly 450,000. [1]
·
· Directly from Africa: About 388,000 captives were shipped directly.
· Via the West Indies (The Inter-American Trade): Between 60,000 and 70,000 enslaved people were transshipped from Caribbean islands like Barbados and Jamaica.
· Thus, mathematically, West Indian imports made up roughly 13.3% to 15.5% of the foundational gene pool. [1, 2]
·
2. The Early "Founder Effect" (1638–1700)
The impact of West Indian slaves is drastically magnified because they arrived first.
·
· Enslaved people coming from Barbados in 1638 (Boston) and 1670 (South Carolina) arrived generations before the peak of the direct trans-Atlantic slave trade to the mainland (which peaked in the mid-to-late 18th century). [3]
· Because they were the "founders" of the colonial enslaved communities, their lineages had an extra 50 to 100 years to multiply compared to Africans who arrived in the late 1700s.
·
3. Natural Population Growth vs. The Caribbean
The demographic trajectory of mainland North America was entirely unique compared to the rest of the Americas: [4]
·
· In the West Indies: Enslaved populations experienced negative growth rates due to brutal labor, disease, and high mortality, requiring constant new imports from Africa. [4, 5]
· In the U.S. Mainland: The enslaved population experienced robust natural self-reproduction. A population that started with a few thousand early colonial laborers (heavily drawn from Barbados) naturally exploded to 4 million people by 1860. [4, 6, 7]
·
4. Regional Concentration in the American South
If you isolate the Deep South, the percentage of descendants spikes dramatically:
·
· In South Carolina and Georgia, the plantation elite ("Goose Creek Men") migrated en masse from Barbados, bringing their enslaved laborers with them.
· Because intermarriage and family blending occurred continuously over 200 years on Southern plantations, it is demographically highly probable that by the onset of the Civil War, nearly every enslaved person in the Lowcountry of South Carolina and Georgia was a direct descendant of those original West Indian cohorts.

text:
The Altar Is Ready-Are We Closer To Renewed Temple Sacrifices Than Most Realize?

By PNW Staff October 06, 2026

For generations, Christians watching developments in Israel have assumed that one enormous event must occur before biblical sacrifices can return to Jerusalem: the Third Temple must first be built.

But what if that assumption is wrong?

According to Rabbi Tovia Singer, one of the most widely followed Jewish teachers in the world, an altar suitable for Temple sacrifices has already been prepared. The priestly garments have been made. Silver trumpets have been fashioned. Other vessels necessary for Temple worship have been recreated.

And according to Singer, the altar is ready to be taken to the Temple Mount.

"We have an altar that's ready to go," Singer recently explained. "It's built. It's here. It's ready to go on the Temple Mount."

Then came the statement that should catch the attention of every student of Bible prophecy:
"You technically do not need a Temple in order for an altar to be placed there and sacrifices to be offered."

That changes the conversation considerably.

For years, prophecy watchers have focused primarily on the enormous political obstacles to rebuilding the Jewish Temple. The Temple Mount contains the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque and remains perhaps the most religiously explosive piece of real estate on earth. Any serious attempt to construct a Jewish Temple there could produce repercussions across the Middle East.

But rebuilding the Temple and resuming sacrifices may not necessarily be the same event.
The biblical precedent is found in Ezra.
When Jewish exiles returned from Babylon to Jerusalem in the sixth century B.C., they found their city devastated and Solomon's Temple destroyed. Yet they did not wait until a new Temple could be constructed before restoring biblical worship.
They built the altar first.
Ezra 3:6 makes the sequence unmistakable:
"From the first day of the seventh month began they to offer burnt offerings unto the LORD. But the foundation of the temple of the LORD was not yet laid."
The Temple wasn't standing.
Its foundation hadn't even been laid.
Yet sacrifices had already begun.
That ancient precedent suddenly makes today's Temple preparations considerably more interesting.
The Altar Is No Longer Theoretical
Organizations connected with the Temple movement have spent decades preparing for a restoration that most of the world considers politically impossible.
But they have not merely held conferences or produced architectural drawings.
The Temple Institute in Jerusalem has recreated numerous vessels associated with biblical Temple worship. Priestly garments have been produced according to extensive study of biblical and rabbinic requirements. A large golden menorah stands prominently in Jerusalem's Old City as a visible symbol of those preparations.
Singer says the altar itself has also been prepared.
Its stones present an unusual challenge because Exodus specifically prohibits using stones shaped by iron tools for an altar.
"If thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast profaned it," Exodus 20:25 declares.
Singer says the stones were therefore prepared without metal touching them.
The symbolism behind the command is striking. Jewish tradition explains that iron represents instruments of warfare and death, while the altar represents reconciliation and atonement. An instrument that shortens life therefore should not be used to construct something intended to preserve it.
Whether one accepts every rabbinic interpretation surrounding the Temple service is beside the point.
The people making these preparations are not building theatrical props.
They intend these objects to be usable.
Preparation Is Not Permission
None of this means sacrifices are about to begin.
Moving an altar onto the Temple Mount would be extraordinarily controversial. The site's religious sensitivities, Israeli government policy, Jordan's custodial role regarding Muslim holy sites and the reaction throughout the Islamic world create enormous obstacles.
An altar can be ready while the political circumstances necessary to use it remain nowhere in sight.
But there is an enormous difference between something being politically impossible and something being physically unprepared.
Political conditions can sometimes change almost overnight.
The physical preparations that might otherwise require years have increasingly already been made.
And that is where these developments become especially significant for Christians interested in Bible prophecy.
You Cannot Stop Sacrifices That Never Started
Several passages in Daniel describe sacrifices being halted.
Daniel 9:27 speaks of someone causing "the sacrifice and the oblation to cease."
Daniel 12:11 similarly describes a time "from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away."
Daniel 8 and Daniel 11 also contain important references to the removal or disruption of regular sacrifices.
Prophecy watchers have long noted an obvious implication: if sacrifices are going to be stopped during future prophetic events, sacrifices must first be taking place.
That has produced a difficult practical question.
How could Israel rebuild an entire Temple, reinstitute the priesthood and establish sacrifices amid the modern political realities surrounding Jerusalem?
Perhaps Ezra provides part of the answer.
The Temple may not have to come first.
That does not eliminate the problem of access to the Temple Mount. But it does alter the potential timeline dramatically.
Instead of imagining that years of Temple construction must necessarily precede the restoration of sacrifice, the biblical precedent demonstrates another possibility:
Altar first.
Sacrifices second.
Temple afterward.
That is exactly what happened following the Babylonian exile.
From Impossible To Conceivable
Consider how dramatically the landscape has changed within little more than a century.
For nearly 2,000 years, the Jewish people had no sovereign state in their ancestral homeland.
Then came 1948.
Jerusalem's Old City and Temple Mount remained outside Israeli control.
Then came 1967.
For decades, Jewish prayer on the Temple Mount was severely restricted, and Jewish visitors were frequently prevented from engaging in visible acts of worship. Yet in recent years, Jewish prayer on the Mount has become increasingly open and visible, even as the official status quo surrounding the site remains extraordinarily sensitive and contested.
Meanwhile, preparations associated with a future Temple have continued.
Priestly garments.
Temple vessels.
Silver trumpets.
Training and research concerning priestly service.
And now the renewed attention surrounding an altar reportedly ready for use.
Each individual development can easily be dismissed as symbolic. Taken together, however, they demonstrate something remarkable.
The infrastructure of an idea is being built before the political opportunity exists.
History has seen that pattern before.
Why Christians Should Be Watching
Jesus specifically directed His followers' attention toward Daniel when discussing events surrounding the end of the age.
"When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place..." He warned in Matthew 24:15.
Paul likewise describes a future figure who "sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God" in 2 Thessalonians 2:4.
Exactly how every prophetic piece fits together remains debated among prophecy scholars.
Twenty-five centuries ago, Jewish exiles returned to a devastated Jerusalem surrounded by hostile peoples.
They did not have a Temple.
They built an altar anyway.
They began offering sacrifices while the Temple remained unbuilt.
Today Jerusalem once again has an altar prepared according to those ancient requirements, according to Singer. Temple vessels have been fashioned. Priestly garments have been sewn. The knowledge necessary for Temple worship is being studied and preserved.
One enormous obstacle remains: the mountain itself.
No one knows when—or whether—the political circumstances surrounding the Temple Mount will change sufficiently for these preparations to be put into practice.
But Christians watching Bible prophecy should recognize how much the question has changed.
For centuries the question was: How could this ever happen?
Increasingly, the question may be: What is still preventing it?
The Temple is not standing.
The sacrifices have not resumed.
But the altar is waiting.

(3) Second Council of Constantinople (A.D. 553)

“If anyone will not confess that the Word of God has two nativities, that which is before all ages from the Father, outside time and without a body, and secondly that nativity of these latter days when the Word of God came down from the heavens and was made flesh of holy and glorious Mary, mother of God and ever-virgin, and was born from her: let him be anathema.”

“If anyone declares that it can be only inexactly and not truly said that the holy and glorious ever-virgin Mary is the mother of God, or says that she is so only in some relative way, considering that she bore a mere man and that God the Word was not made into human flesh in her, holding rather that the nativity of a man from her was referred, as they say, to God the Word as he was with the man who came into being; if anyone misrepresents the holy synod of Chalcedon, alleging that it claimed that the virgin was the mother of God only according to that heretical understanding which the blasphemous Theodore put forward; or if anyone says that she is the mother of a man or the Christ-bearer, that is the mother of Christ, suggesting that Christ is not God; and does not formally confess that she is properly and truly the mother of God, because he who before all ages was born of the Father, God the Word, has been made into human flesh in these latter days and has been born to her, and it was in this religious understanding that the holy synod of Chalcedon formally stated its belief that she was the mother of God: let him be anathema.”

“If anyone defends the letter which Ibas is said to have written to Mari the Persian, which denies that God the Word, who became incarnate of Mary the holy mother of God and ever virgin, became man, but alleges that he was only a man born to her, whom it describes as a temple, as if God the Word was one and the man someone quite different; which condemns holy Cyril as if he were a heretic, when he gives the true teaching of Christians, and accuses holy Cyril of writing opinions like those of the heretical Apollinarius ;which rebukes the first holy synod of Ephesus, alleging that it condemned Nestorius without going into the matter by a formal examination; which claims that the twelve chapters of holy Cyril are heretical and opposed to the true faith; and which defends Theodore and Nestorius and their heretical teachings and books. If anyone defends the said letter and does not anathematize it and all those who offer a defence for it and allege that it or a part of it is correct, or if anyone defends those who have written or shall write in support of it or the heresies contained in it, or supports those who are bold enough to defend it or its heresies in the name of the holy fathers of the holy synod of Chalcedon, and persists in these errors until his death: let him be anathema.”

text:
WHEN LOVE BECOMES A TEMPLE.

There is a love that does not consume. It consecrates.
It does not enter the body as hunger and leave as ash. It arrives as architecture. Slowly, the pulse learns the grammar of pillars. The breath discovers the span of arches. What was once a private ache becomes a nave wide enough for silence to kneel.

In the old mysteries, the temple was never only stone. It was the place where the visible and the invisible agreed to meet without either vanishing. When love reaches that depth, the beloved ceases to be an object of longing and becomes the threshold itself. You no longer reach for them across a distance. You step through them into a sanctum that was always waiting inside the meeting.

The walls are not built of possession. They rise from attention that has stopped bargaining. Every remembered glance is a capital. Every wound that was not turned into a weapon becomes a stained-glass window through which a stranger light enters. The floor is the willingness to remain when the drama has exhausted itself. The altar is the ordinary moment in which two presences refuse to reduce each other to need.

Darkness is not banished here. It is given a place to stand, the way night is given to the sanctuary so that the lamp may be seen. Desire is not denied; it is transfigured into vigil. What once demanded is now offered. What once clutched now holds open.

Love becomes a temple when it stops asking to be saved and begins to shelter. When the heart, no longer a chamber of echoes, becomes a structure in which something holy can dwell without being named, owned, or finished. Those who enter do not leave with answers. They leave carrying a quieter gravity, as if the architecture has rearranged the bones.

And the door, once opened, does not close behind them. It remains, patient as stone, for whoever is ready to stop seeking a feeling and start becoming a place.

Aya, a self-improvement app making $44K/month, has an onboarding flow that is ridiculously long and tedious — but it’s packed with some seriously impressive ideas.

38 screens in total.
• Users have to answer a lot of open-ended questions during onboarding
• At the end, they’re asked: “What do you want to wake up to tomorrow?” and have to answer in 140+ characters
• After all that, before the paywall, the app actually plays a personalized audio experience created based on everything the user entered
• Then a message called “A note from me” appears, written like a personal letter from the Aya team
• Finally, they offer a discounted weekly plan
With onboarding, the key is figuring out how to turn user input into a highly personalized, great experience before the paywall.

That said, onboarding this insanely long can cause major drop-off depending on the category, so you need to be careful.

You can check every onboarding screen and viral social video for Aya on Onbo Hub👇

CYPRUS LEADER TRUMPS UP "MALIGN ACTORS"

President Nikos #Christodoulides hopes to visit #China next year, a herculean task if his Quixotic crusade to protect the West from "malign actors" keeps going viral after it caught the eye of Natalie Harp's team on Truth Social.

The greek cypriot leader recently told #Breitbart News he was glad America was back in his region. But instead of leaving it at that, he went for a Hail Mary for good measure.

"Imagine if we didn’t have a US interest in our neighbors. Who and which actors would be going to fill the vacuum that will be created without the US participation in the region?" Christodoulides asked.

"Malign actors," he answered. 

HOW TO DRAG ON THE RED DRAGON

He didn't name the malign actors. But based on his history, I think he needs to think long and hard before trying to woo China.

Christodoulides was there 11 years ago as government spokesman, with ex-president Nicos Anastasiades on a trip to Shanghai in Fall 2015, when there was interest from #Huawei to build a science and technology park in Limassol. 

Christodoulides' former boss and also at that time foreign minister Ioannis Kasoulides, who had disagreements* on principle with the Paphian native, was oddly left out of that trip.

[*BONUS: check my comment below for their main disagreement]

After then-spokesman Christodoulides met with Victoria "Fuck the EU" Nuland and her neocon gang in Spring 2016, Huawei got the axe and plans were revised so that the Chinese tech giant was kept out. A decade later, the project is still in the air facing serious problems and uncertainty.

HOW TO TURN CYPRUS INTO PALAU

When US President Donald Trump (pronounced Net-an-ya-hu) was getting ready for Israel's attack on Tehran, he started looking for a place to stage American toys, ideally to deter war but practically to shoot down defensive missiles from Iran against Israel and US assets if that were to happen.

Washington asked Lebanon and Beirut said no. 

Then Washington asked Egypt and Cairo said hell no.

But one state, the "Palau" of the eastern Mediterranean, thought it would be cool to offer waters around Cyprus to gang up on Tehran, even if this was an illegal and immoral war against Iran, let alone super dangerous.

CHRISTODOULIDES' TRUMP MATH ISN'T MATHING

I won't get into the other stuff he told Breitbart, but I can summarize them in this paragraph: Christodoulides' apocalyptic fantasies include leading Europe into remaining a vassal continent, encouraging Trump to turn against Erdogan, and forcing the USA to isolate #Turkey from energy plans at a time when Washington desperately tries to keep Ankara at an arm's length from #Russia. 

So I have a piece of advice for Christodoulides, who is widely viewed in Washington DC circles as a neocon showboat that is overcompensating for Trump since the islander pissed him off by arrogantly heeding advice from the greek american lobby to visit Biden's White House only a week before the US election in 2024.

My advice: if you want to visit China next year, you better clarify first in your own head who are the malign actors in your region that you so desperately worry they would fill a vacuum if the US draws back.

Because I have news for you: America is in fact drawing down and this is not yet visible to those with vassal glasses on.

If you really believe in #multilateralism as you say, prove it with a genuine gesture that means you keep your word and show respect when you travel east next year.

If you really believe in sovereignty, then make good choices for your people, don't try to impress bloggers with temporary fashion.

P.S. And a final side note to Breitbart's @mboyle1 Matthew Boyle who conducted the interview with Christodoulides. Matt, I remember you when you joined the war against Washington elitism and corruption. Don't let foreign lobbies use your platform to cross points off a checklist just to impress Trump. That's not what you want. That's not what your president wants.

text:
In my view, what they’re saying can all be valid at a particular point in time. But I wouldn’t blindly apply it across every market environment.

Kelvin Chiu expressed a similar idea in the latest Market Wizards. My takeaway:

Don’t turn a rule that once protected you into dogma that can never be questioned. Rules should evolve with the evidence, your experience, and your ability as a trader.

Take the idea that “when breadth is poor, you should trade less or sit in cash.” 

Over the past two weeks, breadth has been weak, but money has simply been concentrated in semis and the tech indexes. If you focused your trades on that seemingly “narrow” part of the market, making money was actually easier. You didn’t need to keep hunting for new stocks or switching from one name to another.

Another example: “Don’t chase extended stocks.” 

But if a powerful catalyst is driving the move, the next “setup” might form at a higher price and offer a worse entry than buying while the stock looked extended.

Rules are meant to protect traders, not imprison them. When the market, the amount of capital you’re trading, and your own abilities have changed, continuing to treat old rules as unquestionable dogma can itself become a risk.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Mining/Energy/Resources/Biz

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Sports Media Business

AFL reclaims grand final TV crown from NRL
(Original article by Sam Buckingham-Jones)
(Roy Morgan Summary)

Data from OzTAM shows that the Nine Network's coverage of the NRL grand final on Sunday night boasted an average audience of 4.29 million people. Some 1.45 million people also watched the premiership decider via the 9Now app, and the match had a total audience reach of 6.05 million. In contrast, the previous weekend's AFL grand final attracted an average audience of 4.52 million on the Seven Network, and a total audience reach of 6.5 million. Ben Willee from Spinach Advertising says the fact that both codes attracted more than six million viewers underlines the value of live sport for both advertiser and broadcasters. (RMS)

News

Miners stay top of ATO's taxpayer table

(Roy Morgan Summary)
The Australian Taxation Office's latest corporate tax transparency report shows that the nation's largest companies paid $87.5bn in taxes during 2024-25. Rio Tinto topped the list with $5.2bn in taxes, ahead of BHP with a total company tax bill of $3.9bn. The Mining, Energy and Water sector contributed 41.1 per cent of the corporate tax take, or $35.9bn; this was $12.5bn lower than previously, due to weaker commodity prices. The data also shows that the petroleum resource rent tax raised $1.9bn in 2024-25. (RMS)

Netflix chief rules out AI licensing deals

(Roy Morgan Summary)

Netflix's joint CEO Greg Peters has ruled out striking deals to licence technology companies to train their large-language models using the streaming video giant's intellectual property. He notes that many AI platforms are already being trained with Netflix's content, and the company's focus will be on AI models that violate its intellectual property. However, Netflix itself has widely deployed AI technology across its operations, and about 98 per cent of its engineers are now using AI as part of their jobs; Netflix also recently revealed that about 300 of its titles in 2026 have used generative AI at some stage of the production process. Golf's $7bn rebellion collapses: LIV files for bankruptcy

(Orig by Adam Pengilly)

(Roy Morgan Summary)

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil is confident that the rebel circuit will return in 2027, after it filed for bankruptcy protection in a New Jersey court. The move follows the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia's decision to withdraw funding for LIV Golf earlier this year. LIV Golf has secured a deal with private equity firm BC Partners to be an anchor investor for the breakaway league in 2027. However, many players are owed of millions of dollars in overdue payments; they include Australia's Cameron Smith, who signed a $200m deal to join LIV Golf in 2022. Sources have indicated that up to 30 previously contracted golfers have agreed to remain with LIV Golf. (RMS)

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Mining/Energy/Resources/Biz

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

text:
Whole Grains and Your Heart: What 87 Trials Actually Tell Us

A question that took 87 trials to answer

In September 2026 the European Heart Journal published the largest review yet of what happens inside the body when people eat more whole grains. The researchers gathered 87 randomized trials, involving about 6,500 adults across North America, Europe, Asia and Brazil, and asked a simple question that had never been answered with this much data: how much whole grain does it take to move the numbers your doctor watches, and which numbers actually move?

A whole grain, for the purposes of this review, is a kernel with all three of its original layers still present: the fibrous bran on the outside, the nutrient-dense germ at the core, and the starchy endosperm between them. Oats, brown rice, rye, whole wheat and barley all qualify. White rice and white flour do not, because milling has stripped away the bran and germ and left only the starch.

The trials ran anywhere from two weeks to two years, though most lasted about eight weeks, and they compared people eating more whole grain against people eating refined grain, their usual diet, or standard advice. The amounts ranged from a modest 12 grams a day up to more than 200 grams, measured as dry weight before cooking.

What moved, and what barely moved

When all the trials were pooled, almost every marker shifted a little in the right direction. Weight, waist, blood sugar, cholesterol, blood pressure and inflammation all drifted downward in the whole-grain groups. That consistency is the first thing worth noticing, because a pattern that shows up across 87 separate experiments is unlikely to be an accident.

The second thing worth noticing is how small most of those shifts were. The researchers did something that earlier reviews had not: before looking at the results, they set a threshold for each marker, the smallest change that a clinician would consider meaningful for a patient. Then they measured each result against it. Body weight fell by about half a kilogram on average, where a meaningful change would be two and a half. Fasting glucose dropped by roughly one milligram per decilitre, an amount smaller than the morning-to-morning variation on a home glucose meter. Waist circumference narrowed by about six millimetres. HbA1c, the three-month average of blood sugar, moved by five hundredths of a percentage point, below what the laboratory test itself can reliably distinguish.

The lipid picture is different, and this is where the study earns its headline. LDL cholesterol, the particle most tied to arterial disease, fell by a margin the authors judged clinically important, around 0.13 to 0.16 mmol/L depending on the analysis. Total cholesterol and triglycerides followed. Systolic blood pressure, the upper number, came down by roughly two to two and a half points at the most effective intakes, and the inflammatory marker CRP eased by about half a milligram per litre, though the evidence behind the CRP finding is weaker than the rest.

So the honest summary of this review is a two-part sentence. Whole grains reliably nudge nearly every cardiometabolic marker, and for most of those markers the nudge is too gentle to feel. For cholesterol and systolic pressure, the nudge is large enough to matter.

How much, and which grains

The benefits began to appear at around 30 to 40 grams of dry whole grain a day and were strongest for most markers between 60 and 100 grams. In the language of a kitchen rather than a laboratory, that upper range is roughly a bowl of oats in the morning, a slice or two of true whole-grain bread at midday, and a portion of brown rice or barley with dinner. Once the grain is cooked and has absorbed water, 60 to 100 grams dry becomes about 115 to 190 grams on the plate, or four to six of the servings that dietary guidelines count.

Above 100 grams the picture becomes blurry rather than better. Very few trials tested those higher amounts, so the curves widen into uncertainty. HDL cholesterol, the so-called protective fraction, appeared to rise at the highest intakes, but that signal rests on a handful of data points and should be read as a possibility rather than a finding.

The type of grain seemed to matter, though the researchers are careful to call this suggestive. Oats showed the strongest effect on cholesterol, which fits what is already known about beta-glucan, the soluble fibre in oats that binds bile acids in the gut and draws cholesterol out of circulation. Brown rice showed benefits for lipids and inflammation, and rye for waist and weight. These differences likely reflect the different fibres and structures of each grain, and they argue for variety over loyalty to a single source.

What this study cannot tell us

A review like this is only as strong as the trials inside it, and the authors are candid about the limits. Most trials lasted about eight weeks, which is long enough to see cholesterol respond but perhaps too short for weight or blood sugar to tell their full story. Interestingly, the trials that ran longer than four months tended to show smaller effects, not larger ones, which may reflect people drifting back toward old habits, or may simply mean the early benefit fades. The data cannot settle which.

The trials measured risk markers, not heart attacks or strokes. A lower LDL and a lower systolic pressure are genuinely linked to fewer cardiac events over decades, so the inference is reasonable, but it remains an inference. The much larger benefits reported in long-running population studies, where heavy whole-grain eaters have markedly lower rates of heart disease and diabetes, are not fully explained by the modest marker changes seen here. Part of that gap may be cumulative effect over years, part may be that people who eat whole grains differ in other ways the population studies could not fully account for.

There is also the question of what the whole grain was replacing. In most trials it stood in for refined grain, and the strongest results come from exactly those comparisons. The review says nothing about whole grains measured against a diet that contains few grains of any kind, because no trial made that comparison. And many of the included trials had weaknesses of their own: participants knew what they were eating, dropouts were often left out of the analysis, and side effects were rarely tracked carefully enough to say much either way.

Reading it at the table

If you already eat bread, rice or cereal, the clearest lesson of this review is that the whole version of those foods earns its place, and that the gain shows up mainly in your cholesterol and your blood pressure. Swapping white rice for brown, refined bread for a dense whole-grain loaf, or a sweetened cereal for plain oats is a change the trials support, and somewhere between 60 and 100 grams of dry grain a day, spread across the day and drawn from more than one source, is where the evidence is most comfortable.

If your goal is weight, waist or blood sugar, this review asks for patience and perspective. Whole grains will not hurt those numbers, and across thousands of participants they helped a little, but the help was small enough that no one would notice it in a single person. The work on those fronts belongs to the broader shape of your eating, your movement and your sleep, with whole grains as one supporting thread rather than the fabric itself.

And if grains are not a significant part of how you eat, this study offers no reason to begin, because it never asked that question. What it measured was the difference between the whole kernel and the stripped one, and on that narrow but useful point, the whole kernel wins.

LAVV

Source: Naghshi S, Kiani S, Ostadrahimi A, Jayedi A, Mobasseri M, Arefhosseini S, Tutunchi H, Aune D. Whole-grain consumption and cardiometabolic risk: a meta-analysis of randomized trials. European Heart Journal, 2026. doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehag519

🚨 A hospital can now only be paid by the SHA for the services it is actually licensed to provide.

This is the Social Health Authority tightening the rules for the hospitals it contracts under the new 2026 to 2029 cycle. Here is what it means.

The new rule. A health facility will not be allowed to sign a contract with the Social Health Authority for services it is not licensed to offer. Put simply, your contract can only cover what your licence already permits. A facility licensed for outpatient care cannot contract to provide, and bill for, specialist surgery it is not authorised to perform.

The wider shift. The Authority, which runs the national health insurance scheme under the Social Health Insurance Act of 2023, has moved every provider onto fresh contracts running from 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2029. A facility without an executed contract for that cycle cannot serve beneficiaries, its access to the provider portal is switched off, and it must transfer patients already in its care to a contracted provider.

Why this matters legally. Two separate approvals now have to agree. One is the licence, the regulator's permission to offer a given service safely. The other is the contract, the Authority's agreement to pay for it. Lining them up closes a long standing gap, where a facility could bill for services beyond what it was ever cleared to deliver. For patients, it is a safety measure. For facilities, it is a compliance deadline with real financial consequences.

The point worth noting. Public money should pay only for care a provider is lawfully allowed to give, which protects patients and the scheme alike. The harder edge is practical. A facility whose paperwork lags behind its practice can be shut out quickly, and its patients moved, before anyone has tested whether the lockout was fair in a given case.

text:
The Cost of Loyalty: When a Sentinel Puts Down His Gun and Chooses to Speak

A Marine who once took bullets on the battlefield has now turned his weapon on the political one. Jordan Domingue, a decorated combat veteran who served as Chief Security Officer to Abdul El-Sayed, has decided to speak out against his former boss. Domingue stood by the Michigan Senate candidate's side for two years, often 12 to 16 hours a day, armed and vigilant. When he walked away in January, he said: "I regret and feel shame for excusing antisemitism and for not leaving sooner."

This is not partisanship. This is a soldier's last stand for the sake of our national security.

What did Domingue witness? He heard El-Sayed on a leaked campaign call refuse to condemn the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, because "there are a lot of people in Dearborn who are sad today." He watched the candidate respond to a Hezbollah-inspired terrorist attack on a Michigan synagogue, 140 children inside, by saying "hurt people hurt people," blaming Israeli leaders rather than naming Hezbollah, Hamas, or Iran. He saw El-Sayed campaign alongside Hasan Piker, who said "America deserved 9/11" and expressed support for Hamas. He saw him keep close ties to Amer Zahr, a surrogate who told activists to "stop condemning anti-Semitism and condemning terrorism right now."

Domingue could have stayed silent. The campaign offered him money in exchange for a nondisparagement agreement, but he refused. A man who learned loyalty on the battlefield understands where loyalty ends. When loyalty becomes complicity, silence is betrayal.

El-Sayed opposed U.S. funding for Israel's Iron Dome. Domingue personally warned him that Israeli high-rises could collapse under Hamas and Hezbollah rockets. According to Domingue, El-Sayed was indifferent. That shield protects Israel's Muslims, Christians, Druze, and Jews, along with American diplomats, troops, and hundreds of thousands of U.S. visitors.

Domingue didn't just observe. He tried to change El-Sayed's mind. "I thought they were just ignorant and ill-informed," he said. "They turned out to be his beliefs." He accused El-Sayed of "strategic ambiguity" and acting as a "chameleon" on Iran. 

He also exposed a deeper hypocrisy: El-Sayed, who questions whether police should carry guns, employed an armed bodyguard for years. "I protected this man with a gun for two years," Domingue said. "Like so many things with Abdul, it's pure hypocrisy."

The campaign disparaged him after he left their employment. But internal messages confirm he resigned on principle and departed on good terms.

A man who once stood guard with a gun for El-Sayed chose to protect America the most powerful way available, not with a weapon, but with telling the truth. "I wanted to warn people about Abdul," he said, "but it wouldn't be right to do so after taking their money and breaking a commitment."

Domingue's warning is a sentinel's final watch. "Antisemitism is now hidden behind calculated rhetoric," he said, "spoken by people who disguise themselves as partners of peace."

Michigan voters would be wise to heed a man who risked his life for years to protect the very candidate he now warns our nation against as being a danger to this country.
